rationale.conceptual: Established computational methodology (DFT+CHE) applied to a specific system; requires understanding of free‑energy diagrams, zero‑point energy corrections, and construction of several atomic models with fluorination. Not a novel algorithm, but not a trivial black‑box metric.
rationale.execution: Multi‑stage pipeline: building 6 complex atomic models, geometry optimisation of each, then adsorbing 6+ intermediates per catalyst (≈48 DFT runs), collecting energies, and converting via CHE. Orchestration of DFT tool and post‑processing with external thermochemical tables involves 4–5 distinct, dependent stages.

difficulty.reasoning: The underlying work (DFT-based NRR free-energy calculations on fluorinated Fe cluster/graphene models) is standard in computational catalysis, but requires careful model construction, handling of multiple intermediates, and proper application of the CHE model — a non‑trivial but well‑established method. The task pipeline (build models, optimise clean catalysts, compute adsorbed intermediates, post‑process with thermochemical data) spans several dependent stages and tool‑chain (Quantum ESPRESSO, NIST‑JANAF), leading to moderate conceptual and execution difficulty.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Fe65 cluster on 8×8 graphene supercell (~200 atoms) with medium‑cutoff plane‑wave DFT; a single modern GPU suffices for the needed relaxations, input data is trivial (crystal coordinates).
